College Story:

In an airport. 1000 miles from home. After getting my ignition replaced about a week beforehand, so I hadn't had time to get a spare key made (Cadillacs with dealer-issue-only RFID keys). So I had a special locksmith come out who had a contract with Cadillac to make keys, and asked him to disassemble my steering column, take the ignition out, and make two sets of keys. As soon as he removed the airbag it became immediately obvious that the mechanic had stripped the bolt on my steering column when they replaced my ignition, and though they'd gotten it back together, there was no way it was ever going back together if anyone took it apart again. Which meant I had to wait two weeks with no car for a new steering column to be shipped out and installed. Cost me nearly $800.

Six months later my ignition started doing the same thing that led me to replace it the first time around. My next car had plain steel keys and an ignition in the dash I could have apart in five minutes with a crowbar and $50 to have a locksmith rekey it. RFID keys can go suck a goat.
